title: AGENTS.md
text: R/weeknumber-package.R defines constructors calendar constants. Storage double vector week offsets: 0 2000-W01, whose Monday 2000-01-03. Non-finite constructor inputs become NA_real_. R/make_weeknumber.R R/year_week.R convert offsets ISO year/week pairs using 400-year cycle. Preserve ISO week-years New Year; can differ calendar years. Invalid weeks, including week 53 52-week year, become NA. changing conversions arithmetic, cover relevant year boundaries, 53-week years, offsets origin, missing values, empty vectors, vctrs recycling/type behavior. Casting, type compatibility, arithmetic methods live R/cast.R, R/ptype.R, R/arith.R. Scale behavior lives R/scales.R, tests test-scales.R. Default breaks must remain whole visible weeks; n.breaks target, explicit user breaks labels must still work.

code: library(weeknumber) as_weeknumber(c(-1:1, 51:52, NA)) #> <weeknumber[6]> #> [1] 1999-W52 2000-W01 2000-W02 2000-W52 2001-W01 <NA> as_weeknumber("2000-W01") #> <weeknumber[1]> #> [1] 2000-W01 as_weeknumber(as.Date("2000-12-28")) #> <weeknumber[1]> #> [1] 2000-W52 make_weeknumber(2000:2001, 4:5) #> <weeknumber[2]> #> [1] 2000-W04 2001-W05 make_weeknumber(2019:2020, 53) #> <weeknumber[2]> #> [1] <NA>     2020-W53 x <- as_weeknumber(c(-1:1, 51:52, NA)) year_week(x) #> $year #> [1] 1999 2000 2000 2000 2001   NA #>  #> $week #> [1] 52  1  2 52  1 NA set.seed(0) library(tibble) d <- tibble(   x = seq(as_weeknumber("2000-W01"), as_weeknumber("2000-W09")),   y = cumsum(rnorm(length(x))) ) print(d) #> # A tibble: 9 × 2 #>          x     y #>     <week> <dbl> #> 1 2000-W01 1.26  #> 2 2000-W02 0.937 #> 3 2000-W03 2.27  #> 4 2000-W04 3.54  #> 5 2000-W05 3.95  #> 6 2000-W06 2.41  #> 7 2000-W07 1.49  #> 8 2000-W08 1.19  #> 9 2000-W09 1.18 library(ggplot2) p <- ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) +   geom_line() print(p)

title: Position scales for weeknumber vectors — scale_weeknumber
text: helpers use package's weeknumber transformation ggplot2 can plot weeknumber vectors directly format axis labels ISO year-week values. breaks left default, scale chooses regular weekly calendar-aligned interval close n.breaks. Candidate intervals include 1, 2, 4, 8, 13, 26 weeks; quarter, half-year, year starts; sensible multi-year intervals. Calendar-aligned breaks preferred candidates equally close requested number. Consequently, n.breaks target rather guarantee. Supply breaks labels override defaults way ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(). Expansion added ggplot2 excluded default break calculation, ticks remain whole visible weeks.

title: Position scales for weeknumber vectors — scale_weeknumber
code: df <- data.frame(   week = make_weeknumber(2024, 1:6),   value = c(3, 4, 2, 5, 6, 4) )  ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(week, value)) +   ggplot2::geom_line() +   scale_x_weeknumber()   # Request fewer major breaks while retaining calendar-aware spacing. ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(week, value)) +   ggplot2::geom_line() +   scale_x_weeknumber(n.breaks = 3)   ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(value, week)) +   ggplot2::geom_point() +   scale_y_weeknumber()
